name: East Ridge / Inspiration Glacier

pitch_detail.notes: From the col between Pt. 8386 and Dorado Needle. Loose, poorly protectable rock — check every placement. A horn with an existing sling sits ~100 ft up; an alternate start beneath the 'cannonball hole' to the right avoids this section but requires a moat crossing.

Multiple ropelengths along or just below the ridge crest; rock quality improves. Descend into a notch, then traverse the glacier to a ledge marked by quartzite bands (watch for a bottomless moat) to regain the ridge.
Several ropelengths of easier climbing lead to a tower below the true summit.
Two short rappels down into the notch between the sub-summit tower and the summit pyramid.
Two sustained pitches of good-quality 5.7 crack climbing to the summit.

rappel_detail.notes: From the summit area, past old/misleading rappel tat, to a wrapped-block anchor; rappels roughly 30m (~100 ft) down to a stance.

After scrambling easy ledges from the first stance, an approximate, uncomplicated rappel lands in a moatless notch, from which the McAllister-Inspiration col is regained across steep crevassed terrain.

rappels: No single standard rappel line: most parties downclimb/rappel the Northwest Ridge back onto the McAllister Glacier (a few short raps plus a moat crossing); some parties instead make two long rappels (70m rope) straight down the north face to the glacier.
descent_text: From the summit, avoid old/misleading rappel tat and head toward the Northwest Ridge. Locate a wrapped-block rappel anchor a short distance above a stance; rappel roughly 30m (100 ft) to another stance, then scramble easy ledges to a further, uncomplicated rappel that lands in a moatless notch. From there, navigate steep crevasses on climber's right to regain the McAllister-Inspiration col and the glacier route back to camp.
approach: Drive Cascade River Road from Marblemount about 20 miles to the Eldorado Trailhead (~2,100 ft; first 10 miles paved, remainder rough gravel, high-clearance recommended). Hike the Eldorado Trail through forest, cross a creek, and climb steeply to the Eldorado Glacier, then follow the East Ridge of Eldorado Peak to a high camp around 7,400 ft (roughly 4 miles and ~6,000 ft of gain). From camp, rope up and traverse the Inspiration Glacier onto the McAllister Glacier to reach the col at the base of Dorado Needle's East Ridge.
overview: A moderate, remote alpine rock ridge climb on a striking granite spire in the heart of the Eldorado Ice Cap, reached by crossing the Inspiration and McAllister Glaciers from an Eldorado East Ridge high camp, then finishing on two pitches of clean 5.7 crack climbing to the summit.
beta: From the Eldorado East Ridge high camp (~7,400 ft), rope up and cross the Inspiration and McAllister Glaciers to the col between Pt. 8386 and Dorado Needle. The route starts with a loose, thinly-protected 5.5 pitch off the col, eases into several ropelengths of class 3-4 ridge terrain (with a glacier traverse and moat crossing to regain the ridge partway up), then several ropelengths of 3rd-to-low-5th-class climbing to a sub-summit tower. Two short rappels drop into a notch below the true summit, followed by two sustained, high-quality 5.7 pitches to the top. Most parties take 8-12 hours round trip from high camp to summit and back, descending via the technical Northwest Ridge.
fa: Joan and Joe Firey, Hans Hoesli, Dave Knudson, and Peter Renz, July 4, 1971 (attribution uncertain)
